output.headline: Bellingham drives England fightback against world champions Spain
output.standfirst: Jude Bellingham drove a spirited England fightback and James Trafford excelled in goal, but Harry Kane’s missed penalty proved pivotal as Spain, the world champions, won 3-2 at Wembley.
output.bodyHtml:
Thomas Tuchel's England met defeat with none of the recriminations of last time, even as they let a second-half lead slip and lost 3-2 to Spain. The England support can accept losing when their team plays with cut and thrust, and, more to the point, they can accept losing to a Spain side who, at times, played football from a different stratosphere.

Jude Bellingham drove England on, running on adrenaline and playing to the point of maximum expression. England were game throughout and had positive surges either side of the interval, none better than the one towards the end of the first half, when goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put them 2-1 up, hauling them back after Lamine Yamal’s second-minute goal.

Related: Thomas Tuchel denies England players were distracted by Manchester City verdict

England did well to stay within a puncher’s chance of a result in this Nations League opener, and Bellingham was still driving them forward in stoppage time. Crucially, as Tuchel and England look to move on from the heartbreak of the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, there was no negativity from the Wembley crowd, even in the face of defending that was dreadfully loose. The biggest takeaway, though, was Spain’s slickness: there is a reason why they won the World Cup in the summer and the European Championship before that. They are the best team in the international game by a distance, and nobody can live with them.

There were none of the dreaded boos at the full-time whistle. Earlier, in the countdown to kick-off, the reaction to Tuchel’s name went untested: after the starting XI and the 12 substitutes were read out, his name was not announced with the team.

Spain had been the better side for the opening 30 minutes, and when they went again after the Kane penalty, they had too much for England. The match turned on that penalty miss in the 54th minute: had the captain scored, rather than hitting the crossbar after his standing foot gave way in the turf, England would have been 3-1 up. Instead, they were pegged back to 2-2 by the Spain substitute Álex Baena, and there was a degree of inevitability about the winner from another replacement, Mikel Oyarzabal, whose dinked finish was impudently brilliant. It was a statement of intent from Spain, an illustration of their remorseless desire.

“Campeones” was the chant from the enclosure housing the travelling fans before kick-off, and it is fair to say the visiting radio commentators were excited about seeing Spain for the first time since the second star was stitched on to their shirt. Their fervour went up a few notches in the early running when Lamine Yamal opened the scoring.

The goal was a personal disaster for Marc Guéhi; it was almost as if the Manchester City defender had other things on his mind. It was of a piece with England’s struggles against the Spanish press. Guéhi was facing upfield as he tried to build a move from deep but his passing lanes were blocked. So he checked back and walked straight into Lamine Yamal, who robbed him and was clean through. He made the finish past James Trafford look easy.

Trafford has been outstanding for Leeds since joining them over the summer, and he heard the knock of opportunity when Tuchel started him ahead of Jordan Pickford, a major deviation from the head coach’s stated intention for continuity from the World Cup. Pickford had been erratic in the summer and was punished for some of his mistakes. Tuchel’s plan is to share the goalkeeping minutes between Trafford and Pickford during this window, and Trafford repaid the trust by helping to keep England in the game as Spain pushed to add to Lamine Yamal’s goal.

Related: Meet the new 55 minute England collapse, not the same as the old 55 minute England collapse | Barney Ronay

Spain kept pushing. They shimmered with menace, with the movement, the speed of it and the breathtaking assurance on the ball meaning they had so many options in possession that it felt at times as if they had more men on the pitch.

Trafford stood up to make a big one-on-one save from the Spain striker after Lamine Yamal had played the through-ball, while at the other end Ferran Torres had already had the ball in the net, only for it to be ruled out for offside. England’s backline was all over the place, but Trafford made himself big once more when Torres blew another one-on-one chance on 28 minutes, and Dani Olmo rifled just wide after a sumptuous Lamine Yamal flick.

England’s resistance was impressive as they tried to throw counterpunches while hanging on, with Gordon and Bellingham to the fore. They showed their personality when the chips were down, and when the two combined for an equaliser that had not really been advertised, it prompted a wild turnaround.

Spain were pushing again when Nico Williams lost his footing and the ball fell to Elliot Anderson. England swept forward in thrilling style, Gordon flicking to Bellingham, who got the ball back and surged in on goal; the low finish was nerveless.

Kane had his moments: unlucky when he banged a shot inches wide from the edge of the area after a Bukayo Saka burst, then lucky when his header from a Nico O’Reilly cross, which Unai Simón looked to have covered, drew a panicked reaction from Marc Cucurella. The left-back jutted out his thigh and turned the ball past his own goalkeeper. The fates were against Cucurella again when his mishit cross on 45 minutes sailed over Trafford and came back off the far post.

Bellingham appeared particularly determined to leave his imprint. The Real Madrid midfielder was in the mood for bragging rights back in La Liga. It was the power and directness of his running; the smoothness of it, the quickness of his moves. Spain could not contain him. It was his persistence after yet another surge that led to the penalty.

Gordon played the pass back inside from the left and Bellingham got there before Rodri, who invited trouble when he hung out a leg. Down went Bellingham and after a review, it was decided that the contact trumped the feeling that the England player had tried to engineer it. Kane could not convert.

Back came Spain. Lamine Yamal pushed a shot wide after a give and go with Baena, whose backheel was beautiful. Then Baena equalised after O’Reilly gave away the ball and Olmo quickly shifted it to the edge of the area. Baena bought himself the space for the shot with an expert drop of the shoulder.

Saka curled just wide at the other end after more good work by Bellingham but the tide had turned. You could not take your eyes off Lamine Yamal while Luis de la Fuente’s attack-minded changes worked. It was Oyarzabal who made the difference from a Baena pass. England could have no complaints.
output.progress: Thomas Tuchel is rotating James Trafford and Jordan Pickford in goal this window, and Trafford repaid the trust by helping keep England in the game.
